recommendations.body: `resolve_reusable_audit()` in `plan_tool/completeness_report.py` (step 3 "Keep marked checkpoints out of reusable audit lookup") calls `load_review` unguarded inside the new skip-past-unsafe walk, so an unparseable or unsupported-version sidecar raises `ReviewLoadError` out of the lookup rather than being skipped. Because checkpoints are now routinely the newest sidecar, the walk reaches older files that the previous newest-only load never touched — one bad sidecar below a checkpoint aborts the whole `completeness-audit` command, breaking the `_resolve_audit_reuse` contract the detail's `## Input` says to keep (a `None` result declines to a fresh audit, never a failure exit) and contradicting `plan_tool/convergence_diagnosis.py:load_report_history`, which swallows `ReviewLoadError` while applying the same role filter over the same reports directory
recommendations.suggested_action: wrap the per-candidate `load_review` call in `resolve_reusable_audit()` in `try/except ReviewLoadError: continue` so an unloadable sidecar is skipped like an unsafe-role one
